matches.quote: Fig. 3 gives Ω only in units of ω_B F_ac/F_z, so the reader cannot judge whether the "on" state is fast compared with existing Ge HH qubits.
Sn segregation into the well and alloy disorder in the barrier would also shift F*, given the strong x dependence noted for the region boundaries.
Growth feasibility (critical thickness, Sn content and interface) is not addressed. A 15 nm Ge layer under about 2% tensile strain is likely beyond the... critical thickness.

The superconducting-hybrid claims are not supported by any calculation. The abstract and title frame the system as suited to hybrid superconducting-semiconducting devices, but no calculation... is given.
It should also discuss charge-noise dephasing. Near the β-line and the g-lines, dg/dF_z and dΩ/dF_z set qubit coherence
For light holes, coupling to the Γ6 conduction band through the Kane parameter P is the leading correction... recompute β1^p, g⊥^p and g∥^c... with an 8-band model
The validity of the perturbative treatment needs a stated criterion... state how Ω in Fig. 3 was computed: from the effective Hamiltonian (2)... or from a full numerical diagonalization.
The β1 = 0 line is not shown to survive a realistic surface barrier... gives no barrier height, thickness, effective-mass or boundary-condition parameters.
state the corresponding gate voltage and oxide field for a plausible stack, checking against breakdown... discuss the effect of interface traps at a surface where the hole wavefunction resides.
Fig. 1b uses x = 10% while all other results use x = 16%, and the reason is not explained.
In a real device the drive would not vanish exactly, because of: - interface inversion asymmetry and C2v terms... - inhomogeneous strain from gates and thermal mismatch
discuss whether F* ≈ 4.4 V/µm and the g-line fields (about 2 and 7.5 V/µm) can be reached while keeping the dot occupation at one hole;
give absolute Rabi frequencies, for example in MHz for a realistic F_ac at B0 = 0.05 T... compare directly with planar Ge/SiGe HH devices at equal dot size.
whether the β-line is also a dephasing sweet spot (dg/dF_z = 0) is central to the "idle mode" argument.
The novelty relative to Refs. 56 and 57 is not stated. The large linear Rashba term for LH states in Ge/GeSn has already been reported by the same authors.

notes: C13 is marked partly because P5 notes that alloy disorder in the GeSn barrier shifts F* and the LH region boundaries, without explicitly asking if it prevents the LH ground state. C2 is marked partly because P12 and P17 ask to expand on the operational and coherence implications of the beta- and g-lines, though not specifically the leakage argument. C22 is marked partly because P14 questions the accuracy of the perturbative Schrieffer-Wolff expansion versus full diagonalization.
